method.description: Retrieved the three assigned official sources directly from the issuing authority, the Louisiana State Legislature, at the exact article URLs recorded in the acquisition intelligence, plus the controlling article that governs which forms may be used. Extracted each article's form text, hashed it, and read the Acts credit line off the issuer's own page. Compared the result against the identity Edition 1.2 pins for each document.
method.binaryDeposition: The retrieved article pages were written to temporary storage outside the repository for verification and are NOT committed. No file entered version control, no materialization destination was written, and no source-materialization receipt was created. This job's ownedPaths are limited to this single production-factory JSON file.
method.retrievalAgent: curl over HTTPS, Chrome 126 user-agent string, redirects followed, 45s timeout
method.extractionProcedure:
For arts. 986, 993 and 998 the article body was taken as the balanced
subtree of the response. For art. 995 the body is not wrapped in that div and was taken from the ctl00_PageBody_LabelDocument span. In both cases
and

were converted to newlines, remaining tags stripped, HTML entities unescaped, runs of spaces and non-breaking spaces collapsed to one space, and runs of three or more newlines collapsed to two, then leading and trailing whitespace trimmed.
method.digestCaveat: retrievedPageSha256 is NOT a stable identity. legis.la.gov is an ASP.NET WebForms application and every response carries a fresh __VIEWSTATE, so the whole-page digest changes between requests of the same unchanged article. It is recorded as a provenance fact about this single retrieval. normalizedTextSha256 is stable across retrievals for unchanged text, but it is a digest of an extraction performed by this job under the procedure above; it is a working provenance digest, not a pinned authority identity, and it must not be adopted as an edition identity without an independent extraction.

controllingAuthority.article: La. C.Cr.P. art. 986 — Forms for the expungement of records

operativeTextVerbatim.A: Only the forms provided for in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995, and 998 shall be used for filing motions to expunge a record of an arrest which did not result in a conviction, for the expungement of a record of arrest and conviction of a misdemeanor or felony offense, or for an interim motion to expunge a felony offense which resulted in a misdemeanor conviction.
operativeTextVerbatim.B: Supplemental forms may be added to any petition as long as they adhere to the form provided for in Article 993 of this Code.
operativeTextVerbatim.C: The clerk of court for any court in the state of Louisiana having criminal jurisdiction may amend any of the forms provided for in Articles 987, 988, 989, 990, 991, 992, 993, 994, 995, and 998 to provide the appropriate name of the court ordering an expungement of records.

whatThisEstablishes: There is no issuing forms office in Louisiana for this family. The statutory text IS the form, and art. 986(A) makes it mandatory and exclusive.
Scope is statewide and the only permitted local variation is the court's name, under art. 986(C). No parish, city or district may substitute its own version.
Art. 993 governs supplemental sheets: a supplemental form is permitted only if it adheres to the art. 993 form.
Art. 998 is inside the exclusive list, added when Acts 2023 No. 342 amended art. 986 and enacted art. 998 in the same act.

formStructureObserved.whyItMatters: The Louisiana Supreme Court's city and parish packet splits the sheet into three fillable variants. That is a rendering convention of a non-mandatory packet, not the statute. A field map keyed on three documents where the statute has one will misrepresent the filing.

revisionLabelFinding.headline: SOURCE-2026-07-31 is a capture date, not an issuer revision. The currentness question as posed cannot be answered because it asks about a value the issuer never published.
revisionLabelFinding.recordedQuestion: The source-acquisition queue asks, on all six affected rows, 'Confirm SOURCE-2026-07-31 is still the issuer's current revision.'
revisionLabelFinding.why: The Louisiana State Legislature does not version these articles by revision number or form-face date. Their only versioning mechanism is the Acts credit line printed at the foot of the article. SOURCE-2026-07-31 records when a copy was taken, which says nothing about what the issuer published.
revisionLabelFinding.corroboratedBySiblingConvention: Edition 1.2 already pins the six sibling articles in this family on exactly this basis: art. 987 ACTS-2014-145, art. 988 ACTS-2015-200, art. 989 ACTS-2020-73, art. 991 ACTS-2014-145, art. 992 ACTS-2024-580, art. 994 ACTS-2018-711. Only these three carry a capture-date label, and only these three are classed source_gated rather than packet_form.
revisionLabelFinding.currentnessAnswer: As of 2026-08-07 the Legislature publishes each of the three articles with the Acts credit line recorded above, and each credit line is byte-identical to the one read on 2026-08-03. No later amending act appears for any of them. The text is current.
revisionLabelFinding.whatIsNotEstablished: That the held source-gated PDF's bytes reproduce that current text. The held copies are under private/, absent from this worktree, and this job is not authorized to materialize them. Text currentness is established; held-copy fidelity is not.

doNotSubstitute.source: Louisiana Supreme Court, Uniform Forms for City & Parish Courts
doNotSubstitute.negativeFinding: This packet contains fillable supplemental sheets and an interim-expungement order and is an official Louisiana Supreme Court publication, so it is tempting. It must not be substituted for the statutory forms. It is expressly non-mandatory and limited to city and parish courts, while art. 986(A) makes the statutory forms exclusive statewide and art. 986(C) permits only the court's name to be amended. It also splits the single art. 993 supplemental sheet into three fillable variants and omits art. 998 entirely. Availability in PDF is not authority.

Both are 'Motion for Expungement' forms and both are primary filings. Art. 989 is the general motion used by la-976, la-977, la-978 and la-985-expungement-by-redaction; art. 998 is the narrow first-offense-marijuana misdemeanor motion used only by la-977d. They must not be interchanged.

All three are orders. Arts. 991 and 992 are the order forms for the general expungement tracks; art. 995 is the order of expungement of an interim arrest record and belongs only to la-985-1-interim-expungement. Role identity is not enough — the order must match its motion.

Adjacent numbers in the same interim-expungement track. Art. 994 is the motion for interim expungement (primary_filing); art. 995 is its order (proposed_order). Motion and order must never be swapped.
Art. 990 is inside the art. 986(A) exclusive list but is bound to no component in any assigned track. Its presence in the statutory list is not a reason to bind it.

Louisiana expungement forms are republished as fillable derivatives by commercial vendors and parish clerk sites. None is a controlling source. Art. 986(A) admits only the statutory forms, and no derivative may establish text, revision or scope.

retrievedPageSha256 must not be pinned as an identity. The __VIEWSTATE token changes on every request, so a second retrieval of unchanged text yields a different page digest. Treating a page digest as an identity would manufacture a false supersession on the next check.
